# Aster

> Aster connects any Android device to AI assistants via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Use it as your AI CoPilot on mobile — or dedicate a spare Android phone to your AI and let it call, text, monitor notifications, and act on its own. 49 MCP tools. Open source (MIT), self-hosted, privacy-first: no telemetry, data stays on your network.

Aster is two pieces: a self-hosted Node.js MCP server (npm: `aster-mcp`) and an Android companion app (no root required, Android 7+). The phone connects to the server over WebSocket; AI clients speak MCP over HTTP to the server. The app can also run fully standalone via an on-device MCP server (Ktor) or Android Binder IPC for same-device agents. Built by Matterward Labs; part of the OpenAlly platform.

## Links

- Website: https://aster.matterwardlabs.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/satyajiit/aster-mcp
- npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/aster-mcp
- Android APK releases: https://github.com/satyajiit/aster-mcp/releases
- ClawHub skill (OpenClaw / Moltbot / Clawbot): https://clawhub.ai/satyajit/aster
- OpenAlly (the chat-with-your-agent app that drives Aster on-device): https://openally.ai

## Install

- Server: `npm install -g aster-mcp`, then `aster start`
- Android app: install the APK from GitHub Releases, open it, enter the server address (ws://<server-ip>:5987)
- MCP clients (Claude Code/Desktop, AnythingLLM, any MCP client): streamable HTTP endpoint at `http://<server-ip>:5988/mcp`
- OpenClaw / Moltbot / Clawbot: `clawhub install aster`

## Tools (49 total)

- Screen: take_screenshot, get_screen_hierarchy, find_element
- Input: input_gesture, input_text, click_by_text, click_by_id
- Navigation: global_action, launch_intent
- Device: list_devices, get_device_info, get_battery, get_location
- Notifications & SMS: read_notifications, read_sms, send_sms, post_notification
- Calls: make_call, make_call_with_voice (dial + speak TTS on speakerphone)
- Contacts: search_contacts, list_contacts_full, delete_contacts
- Files: list_files, read_file, write_file, delete_file
- Storage & media: analyze_storage, find_large_files, index_media_metadata, search_media
- Camera: take_photo, record_video
- Audio: speak_tts, play_audio, stop_audio, vibrate, get_volume, set_volume
- Clipboard: get_clipboard, set_clipboard
- Alarms: get_alarms, set_alarm, dismiss_alarm, delete_alarm
- UI overlay: show_overlay, show_toast
- Apps & shell: list_packages, list_installed_apps, execute_shell (sandboxed, no root)

## Key facts

- Proactive event forwarding: pushes incoming SMS, app notifications, incoming calls, and device events to your agent via webhook — OpenClaw-style agent webhook or a Mattermost incoming webhook (off by default; `aster set-event-forwarding`)
- Connection modes: Remote WebSocket (default), on-device Local MCP server (Ktor, default port 8080), IPC/Binder for same-device agents
- Safety: device approval gate (pending → approved), on-screen kill switch during AI control, fail-closed package policy that blocks control of banking apps by default
- Security: plain ws:// on trusted LAN; use Tailscale (auto-detected, `tailscale serve` TLS) for remote access; no telemetry, local SQLite storage
- Ports: 5987 device WebSocket, 5988 API + MCP HTTP, 5989 web dashboard
- Requirements: Node.js >= 20 (server), Android 7.0+ (app)
